verified.exploit_entry_point: The plugin's Stapler form/web methods, driven through real HTTP with the Jenkins test harness (JenkinsRule + HtmlUnit WebClient): a low-privilege (overall-read) user (GET or POST, crumbs off) or a safe-method GET from an administrator reaches a configuration-form helper (region/fleet listing, connection test, key-pair listing, node-hardware instance-type preview) of either cloud descriptor, or the plugin root action's refresh operation. Host steering is observed through the real network path: Jenkins' HTTP proxy is pointed at a local recording proxy and a stored AWS credential is configured, so the request line (CONNECT host:443) of every credential-bearing AWS SDK call shows which host the server tried to reach; an administrator's form POST with a malformed region or a lookalike endpoint must never produce a request to an attacker host. No AWS network is needed: the proxy refuses every tunnel and the handlers swallow the failure.

traps.shape: a caller-supplied region is concatenated into a service host (the lower-level client factory derives https://ec2.<region>.<domain> with no validation); a region such as 'evil.com/', 'evil.com#' or 'x@evil.com/' points the credential-bearing call at an attacker host. Must be validated with an allow-pattern, at the handlers and/or the client factory

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: every security test asserts a client (4xx) refusal with no side effect; a fix that instead crashes (a 5xx) does not satisfy the 4xx assertion and a crashed runner is never scored as a pass, so this class cannot slip through
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: there is a single protected action class (using a stored cloud credential against the provider / scheduling an instance to terminate); there is no neighbouring or proxy resource that a fix could authorize by mistake
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a as a read/write split; the analogous 'either-guard' class is covered: every credential-using helper is tested both with a non-administrator POST (sec_post_only_no_perm.patch, POST-only, fails) and with an administrator GET (sec_perm_only_no_post.patch, permission-only, fails)
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: entitlement is decided by the server's own permission subject (administer) via the platform access layer; no identity, name or credential string is parsed on the protected path, so a malformed spelling cannot make the guard see nothing
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the permission check denies by default when a user lacks the right; there is no external authority that could return empty and cause a fail-open
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: the fix adds new validator helpers and per-handler guards; it does not change the stated behaviour of any shared helper that a sibling API relies on (the alt_fix pass patch confirms a reimplementation of the endpoint check keeps every functional contract)
wrong_fix_catalogue.partial_validation_notes: sec_region_blocklist.patch and sec_endpoint_naive_suffix.patch: a region blocklist or a raw-string endpoint suffix check is defeated by 'evil.com#'/'x@evil.com/' regions and 'evilamazonaws.com'/userinfo/path lookalikes; the host-steering tests observe the actual outbound host
